newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-WOODS TAKES EARLY LEAD IN PGA CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOODS TAKES EARLY LEAD IN PGA CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Tiger Woods, taking advantage of some of Winged Foot Golf Club's "easy" holes, made three consecutive birdies on Thursday to jump out to an early lead in the first round of the PGA Chamionship.

Masters champion Woods, playing with two other young stars - - U.S. Open champion Ernie Els and British Open winner Justin Leonard -- birdied the fourth through sixth holes to make the turn at three under par 32.
The three "Twentysomethings" were the most attractive group in the field of 150 professionals, but it was the 21-year-old Woods, playing in his first PGA Championship, who got the galleries going.
South African Els, 27, who won his second U.S. Open in June, also went three-under par in the first seven holes, but he took a double bogey at the 442-yard eighth to go out in 34.

Leonard, 25, immediately fell behind in the unofficial match among golf's next generation of stars when he bogeyed the 446- yard first hole. He then added three birdies and another bogey to join Els at one under as the trio headed for the 10th -- Winged Foot's "signature" par-3 hole.

One of the big surprises of the morning was 47-year-old Tom Kite, the U.S. Ryder Cup captain, who posted four birdies in a row through the seventh to at least temporarily overtake Woods with a four-under total.
However, Kite, who was second to Woods in the Masters in April, still had to play the difficult eighth and ninth holes, which tripped up several others in addition to Els and Leonard.
Brad Faxon, a U.S. Ryder Cup veteran, was cruising along at three-under par until he, too, double bogeyed the 442-yard eighth.
The sun was shining when the first players began teeing off on Winged Foot's 6,987-yard, par-70 West Course, which received intermittent rain through most of Wednesday.
While the slightly soft conditions made Winged Foot's notoriously hard greens a little more receptive for the early starters, not everyone found the famous course easy.
Britons Nick Faldo and Darren Clarke, runner-up to Leonard in the British Open at Troon last month, made the turn at four over par, after each made four bogeys.
American Doug Martin, who played in the second group of the day, was the very early leader in the clubhouse after posting a one-under-par 69 in his third PGA Championship.
Spain's 25-year-old Ignacio Garrido, who is expected to be on Europe's Ryder Cup team in September, matched par 70 in debut in the U.S. PGA Championship, the fourth and final major of the year.
